privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains what information OYNO collects, how we use it, and the choices you have. By using OYNO, you agree to the practices described here.

sections.heading: Information we collect
sections.body: When you create an account, we collect the name and email address you provide, or — if you sign in with Google or Apple — the name and email those providers share with us. We also store your in-app progress: XP, level, coins, gems, streaks, achievements, and the cultural content you've unlocked. We do not collect payment details, government ID, or precise location.

sections.heading: How we use your information
sections.body: We use this information to create and secure your account, save and sync your progress across devices, show your rank on leaderboards (unless you set your profile to private in Settings > Privacy), send you notifications you've opted into, and improve OYNO based on how the app is used.

sections.heading: Signing in with Google or Apple
sections.body: When you continue with Google or Apple, we receive only your name, email address, and a unique identifier for your account — never your password. Apple may provide a private relay email address if you choose to hide your email; we treat it the same as any other email on file.

sections.heading: Sharing your information
sections.body: We do not sell your personal information. It is stored with Supabase, our database and authentication provider, under a data processing agreement. We share information with Google or Apple only as part of the sign-in flow you initiate. We may disclose information if required by law.

sections.heading: Data retention and deletion
sections.body: We keep your account data for as long as your account is active. You can permanently delete your account and its data at any time from Settings > Account > Delete account. Some records may be retained briefly afterward where required for security or legal reasons.

sections.heading: Children's privacy
sections.body: OYNO is designed to be family-friendly, but it is not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13 without a parent or guardian's consent. If you believe a child has created an account without consent, contact us and we will delete it.

sections.heading: Your rights
sections.body: You can review and update your name and email in Settings > Account, control who sees your profile and activity in Settings > Privacy, and request a copy or deletion of your data by contacting us.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: We use industry-standard measures, including encrypted connections and Supabase's row-level security, to protect your data. No method of transmission or storage is completely secure, so we can't guarantee absolute security.

sections.heading: Changes to this policy
sections.body: We may update this policy as OYNO grows. If we make material changes, we'll let you know in the app before they take effect.

sections.heading: Contact us
sections.body: Questions about this policy? Email us at support@oyno.app.

termsOfUse.title: Terms of use
termsOfUse.intro: These Terms of Use govern your access to and use of OYNO. By creating an account or using the app, you agree to these terms.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.body: You must be able to form a binding agreement to use OYNO. If you are under 13, please use OYNO together with a parent or guardian.

sections.heading: Your account
sections.body: You're responsible for the activity on your account and for keeping your password confidential. Guest mode lets you explore without an account, but your progress won't be saved.

sections.heading: Acceptable use
sections.body: Don't use OYNO to harass others, cheat, exploit bugs, attempt to access another user's account, or interfere with the app's normal operation.

sections.heading: Content and cultural material
sections.body: OYNO's illustrations, games, and cultural content are provided for learning and entertainment. We aim for cultural accuracy, but OYNO is not a substitute for academic or historical sources.

sections.heading: In-app currencies
sections.body: Coins, gems, and XP are virtual items with no real-world monetary value. They cannot be exchanged for cash and may be adjusted, reset, or removed as the app evolves.

sections.heading: Intellectual property
sections.body: OYNO's design, artwork, and code belong to us or our licensors. You may not copy, redistribute, or reuse them outside the app without permission.

sections.heading: Termination
sections.body: You may delete your account at any time in Settings. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate these terms.

sections.heading: Disclaimer
sections.body: OYNO is provided "as is." We work hard to keep it accurate and available, but we don't guarantee it will be error-free or uninterrupted.

sections.heading: Changes to these terms
sections.body: We may update these terms as OYNO changes. Continued use after an update means you accept the revised terms.

sections.heading: Contact us
sections.body: Questions about these terms? Email us at support@oyno.app.

tunduk-flag.question: What is shown on Kyrgyzstan's state flag?
tunduk-flag.explanation: The tunduk is a symbol of Kyrgyz national identity - it appears on the state flag.

tunduk-parts.question: The tunduk has two parts: the alkak (outer ring) and…?
tunduk-parts.explanation: The crossed lattice inside the alkak is called the chamgarak.

tunduk-position.question: The tunduk sits at the bottom of the boz uy's wall.
tunduk-position.explanation: No - the tunduk is the round smoke opening at the top of the roof, the most sacred part of the home.

kerege-wall.question: Which part of the boz uy's wooden frame works as the wall?
kerege-wall.explanation: The kerege is the lattice frame that forms the wall; the uuk poles run from the kerege up to the tunduk.

tuurduk.question: What is the felt that covers the kerege called?
tuurduk.explanation: The tuurduk covers the kerege; the üzük are the large front and back felt pieces.

tor.question: What is the most honoured place behind the hearth called?
tor.explanation: The tör is the place of honour, kept for the head of the family or a respected guest.

image-tunduk.question: Which picture shows a tunduk?
image-tunduk.explanation: The tunduk is the round opening at the top of the boz uy's roof.

kok-boru-unesco.question: Kök Börü was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2017.
kok-boru-unesco.explanation: True - it was inscribed in December 2017.

kok-boru-rules.question: Who developed Kök Börü's modern unified rules in 1996?
kok-boru-rules.explanation: They were developed by film director Bolot Shamshiev.

kyz-kuumai.question: What does the game Kyz kuumai show?
kyz-kuumai.explanation: Kyz kuumai shows a girl's riding skill - a Kyrgyz girl was expected to ride as well as any young man.

options.yurt: How fast a yurt is built

kymyz.question: Which drink is made from the milk of the Kyrgyz horse?
kymyz.explanation: The horse gave meat, milk (kymyz), hide and strength.

hooves.question: Kyrgyz horses have hooves so strong they need no shoeing, even on long journeys.
hooves.explanation: True - it can also graze year-round and get through winter on little hay.

saddle-dowry.question: A decorated saddle was once given as part of a bride's dowry.
saddle-dowry.explanation: True - a saddle showed its owner's standing and taste.

image-kok-boru.question: Which picture shows Kök Börü?
image-kok-boru.explanation: Kök Börü is the game where the unity of horse and rider shows most clearly.

shyrdak-unesco.question: In which year was the craft of shyrdak and ala-kiyiz added to UNESCO's list?
shyrdak-unesco.explanation: In 2012 - to the Intangible Cultural Heritage list.

shyrdak-edges.question: What do the white-and-black edges of a shyrdak stand for?
shyrdak-edges.explanation: The edges always finish in white and black - the snowy peaks of the Kyrgyz mountains.

shyrdak-blue.question: In a shyrdak, what does blue stand for?
shyrdak-blue.explanation: Blue is Tengri's sacred colour - the sky and the cosmos. White means purity, yellow wealth.

kochkor-muyuz.question: The kochkor müyüz (ram's horn) element sets Kyrgyz ornament apart from other peoples' ornament.
kochkor-muyuz.explanation: True - no pattern is made without the kochkor müyüz.

umai-ene.question: Umai Ene is traditionally seen as the protector of…?
umai-ene.explanation: Umai Ene is the sacred mother seen as protector of children and childbirth.

komuz-strings.question: How many strings does the komuz have?
komuz-strings.explanation: The komuz is the oldest Kyrgyz three-stringed plucked instrument.

komuz-kashgari.question: The komuz is mentioned in Mahmud Kashgari's 11th-century dictionary, Dīwān Lughāt al-Turk.
komuz-kashgari.explanation: True - it appears in that 11th-century dictionary.

son-kol-altitude.question: How high above sea level is Son-Köl?
son-kol-altitude.explanation: Son-Köl lies at 3,016 m, in Naryn Region.

sary-chelek-depth.question: Sary-Chelek is Kyrgyzstan's deepest lake after Issyk-Kul.

lenin-peak.question: The highest peak of the Chong Alay range is Lenin Peak (7,137 m).
lenin-peak.explanation: True. The Achik-Tash alpine camp is here too.

arslanbob-forest.question: Arslanbob is known for the world's largest… forest?
arslanbob-forest.explanation: Arslanbob is the world's largest walnut forest - some trees are over a thousand years old.

suusamyr-valley.question: Suusamyr is a high mountain lake.
suusamyr-valley.explanation: No - Suusamyr is a wide summer-pasture valley, a main grazing land for livestock.

image-son-kol.question: Which picture shows Son-Köl?
image-son-kol.explanation: Son-Köl is a high mountain lake formed by glaciers.
